questions.question: ______ was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a part of the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sukanya Samridhi Account.**__

 
• Inaugurated in 2015, Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is a small deposit scheme of the Government of India meant exclusively for a girl child.
 
• It was launched as a part of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Campaign.
 
• The scheme, governed by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, is meant to meet the education and marriage expenses of a girl child.

questions.question: The coil of wire in an electric room heater or electric cooking heater is called _______.
questions.solution:
• The coil of wire in an electric room heater or electric cooking heater is called a **metal heating element**.
 
• Most heating elements use nichrome 80/20 (80% nickel, 20% chromium)wire.
 
• Nichrome 80/20 is an ideal material for heating elements owing to its high resistance and formation of an adherent layer of chromium oxide when heated for the first time.

questions.question: In 1916 Mahatma Gandhi travelled to_______ to inspire the peasants to struggle against the oppressive plantation system.
questions.solution: In 1916, the British rulers were forcing many tenant farmers in Champaran to grow indigo on their land as a condition of their tenancy. Mahatma Gandhi travelled there and inspired the peasants to struggle against this oppression. His encouragement led to the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, the first Satyagraha movement inspired by Gandhi.

questions.question: The land mass of India has an area of _______ million square km.
questions.solution: The geographical extent of India lies from 8⁰4' N to 37⁰6' N latitudes and 68⁰ 7' E to 97⁰25' E longitudes. The area of India’s landmass is 3.287 million square km.

questions.question: "Betting and gambling" is listed in the _______ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.solution: According to the 7th Schedule of the Constitution of India (entry no. 40 of List I and entry nos. 34 and 62 of List II), the Union government is empowered to make laws to regulate the conduct of lotteries, while the State Governments are responsible for authorising/conducting the lotteries and making laws on betting and gambling.

questions.question: Who created the first mechanical computer, which proved to be the prototype for future computers?
questions.solution: The idea of a digital programmable computer was originated by English polymath Charles Babbage for the first time. In 1822, Charles Babbage conceptualized and began developing the Difference Engine, considered to be the first automatic computing machine.

questions.question: To whom the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2016 was awarded?
questions.solution: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2016 was awarded to Yoshinori Ohsumi for the discovery of mechanisms underlying autophagy, a fundamental process for degrading and recycling cellular components.

questions.question: _______ is obtained by evaporation of seawater.
questions.solution:
• Evaporation of seawater leaves salt behind.
 
• Salt evaporation ponds, also called salterns, salt works or salt pans, are shallow artificial ponds into which seawater or brine is fed and water is drawn out through natural evaporation which allows the salt to be subsequently harvested.

questions.question: ______ is separated from India by a narrow channel of sea formed by Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar.
questions.solution: Sri Lanka lies in the Indian Ocean southwest of the Bay of Bengal, between 5° and 10°N latitudes, and 79° and 82°E longitudes. It is separated from the mainland portion of the Indian subcontinent by the Gulf of Mannar and Palk Strait. Adam’s Bridge, also known as Rama Setu, separates Palk Strait from the Gulf of Mannar.

questions.question: Which of the following river originates in Nepal and flows into the Ganges?
questions.solution:
The river__** Kosi**__, also known as Saptakoshi due to its seven tributaries, originates in Nepal and courses towards Bihar where it joins the Ganga south of Purnea.

Kosi has long been notorious for its devastating floods due to the frequent shifting of its course that is attributed to the youthful topography of the river.

**It is known as the Sorrow of Bihar.**

questions.question: ______ software are freely available and can be edited and customized by anyone.
questions.solution: The term "open source" refers to software which people can modify and share because its design is publicly accessible. The source code, i.e. the code computer programmers manipulate to change how the software works, of an open source software can be inspected and modified by anyone.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from _______ in January 1915.
questions.solution: Prior to 1915, Mahatma Gandhi was settled in South Africa, working for rights for black South Africans through passive resistance. At the request of Gopal Krishna Gokhale, conveyed to him by C. F. Andrews, Gandhi returned to India on 9th January, 1915.

questions.question: In which sport did India win Bronze medal at Rio Olympics 2016?
questions.solution: Indian wrestler Sakshi Malik clinched the bronze medal in women's wrestling 58 kg category at Rio Olympics 2016.

questions.question: According to Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, with spending of $55.9 Billion in 2016, which country became world’s fifth-largest military spender?
questions.solution: India is the 5th largest military spender in the world, behind USA, China, Saudi Arabia and Russia. In 2017, India’s military spending amounted to 63.9 billion dollars, i.e. 2.5% of the GDP.

questions.question: Ajanta and Ellora caves are situated in which state of India?
questions.solution:
• Located 100 kms apart from each other, Ajanta and Ellora caves are situated in the state of Maharashtra.
 
• The Ajanta Caves are 29 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments which date from the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE.
 
• The Ellora cave complex features Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments dating from the 600-1000 CE period.

questions.question: ______ being a higher category, is the assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Order**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The eight main taxonomic ranks are:
 
 
• Domain
 
• Kingdom
 
• Phylum or division
 
• Class
 
• Order
 
• Family
 
• Genus and
 
• Species.
 
 
 
• Each step down in the classification divides organisms into more and more specific groups.
 
• Order is the taxonomic category which groups families that exhibit similar characteristics.

 
• Biologists, such as Ernst Haeckel, Robert Whittaker, and Carl Woese tried to classify all living organisms into broad categories called kingdoms.
 
• Further classification is done by naming the sub-groups at various levels- kingdom, phylum or division, class, order, family, genus, species.
 
• This is also known as the Taxonomic hierarchy.
 
• Taxonomic hierarchy - It is the process of arranging various organisms into successive levels of the biological classification either in a decreasing or an increasing order from kingdom to species and vice versa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kingdom - It is the highest level of classification. 
 
• There are 5 kingdoms in which the living organisms are classified, namely, Animalia, Plantae, Fungi, Protista, and Monera.
 
• Phylum - Organisms in a phylum share a set of characteristics that distinguishes them from organisms in another phylum. In botany, the term division has been used instead of the phylum.
 
• Class - Class was the most general rank in the taxonomic hierarchy until phyla were not introduced. Kingdom Animalia includes 108 classes.
 
• Order - It constitutes one or more than one similar family.
 
• Family - It includes various genera that share a few similarities.
 
• Genus - A group of similar species forms a genus.
 
• Species - It refers to a group of organisms that are similar in shape, form, and reproductive features. There are about 8.7 million different species on earth.

questions.question: If the _______ firm has zero costs or only has fixed cost, the quantity supplied in equilibrium is given by the point where the marginal revenue is zero.
questions.solution: If the monopoly firm has zero costs or only has fixed cost, the quantity supplied in equilibrium is given by the point where marginal revenue is zero. In contrast, perfect competition would supply an equilibrium quantity given by the point where average revenue is zero.

questions.question: Sexual reproduction in Algae that takes place through fusion of two dissimilar size gametes is called?
questions.solution: Anisogamy, also known as heterogamy, is the form of sexual reproduction which involves the union or fusion of two gametes, which differ in size and/or form. In anisogamy, both gametes can be flagellated and therefore, motile or both may be non-flagellated. This latter condition occurs in some algae and plants.

questions.question: The passage of an electric current through a conducting liquid causes _______.
questions.solution: Most liquids that conduct electricity are solutions of acids, bases and salts. When current is passed through a conducting liquid it causes chemical reactions. The resulting effects are called chemical effects of current.

questions.question: The short run marginal cost curve is _______ shaped.
questions.solution: In economics, short-run marginal cost is an economic concept that describes the cost of producing a small quantity of additional units of a good or service. The short-run marginal cost (MC) curve is U shaped. It first declines and then goes up at some point, and intersects the average total cost and average variable cost curves at their minimum points.

questions.question: There are total ______ parliamentary seats (Lok Sabha constituency) in West Bengal.
questions.solution: West Bengal has the third highest number of Parliamentary seats out of all the states and union territories. It possesses 42 seats, behind UP (80) and Maharashtra (48).

questions.question: The animals in which the body cavity is absent are known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acoelomates.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The animals in which the body cavity is absent are known as **Acoelomates.**
 
• Example - flatworms and tapeworms, 
 
• **Acoelomates** lack a fluid-filled cavity between the body wall and digestive tract. They exhibit bilateral symmetry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coelom **is the principal body cavity in most animals, located between the intestinal canal and the body wall. 
 
• **Coelomates** refers to the animals having fluid-filled body cavities called coeloms located within the **mesoderm**.
 
• There are three different tissues layers (**ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm**). The cells in each tissue layer become differentiated during development, becoming different tissues, organs, and a digestive tract.
 
• **Pseudocoelomates** refers to animals having fluid-filled body cavity between endoderm and the mesoderm. **Pseudocoelom **means **"false coelom"** or **"false cavity"**
 
• **Wild **refers to any living organism in its natural environment without interference of human beings.

questions.question: ______ is the number of individuals of the population who left the habitat and gone elsewhere during the time period under consideration.
questions.solution: The size of the population in a habitat keeps changing with time, depending on various factors including food availability, predation pressure and weather conditions. Immigration is the number of individuals of the same species that have come into the habitat from elsewhere during the time period under consideration. Emigration is the number of individuals of the population who left the habitat and gone elsewhere during the time period under consideration.

questions.question: According to the Second Law of Motion, for a given force, acceleration is inversely proportional to the _________ of an object.
questions.solution: Newton's second law of motion states that, “The acceleration of an object as produced by a net force is directly proportional to the magnitude of the net force, in the same direction as the net force, and inversely proportional to the mass of the object”.
